sections.title: Identity and form
sections.text: This catalogue entry depicts the cultivated garden pea, Pisum sativum. Some current taxonomic treatments place that name in synonymy with Lathyrus oleraceus, while horticultural references continue to use P. sativum. The annual climbing plant bears tendrils and grows roughly 0.45–1.8 m, depending on the cultivar.

sections.title: Flowers and pods
sections.text: The papilionaceous flowers are usually white, pink or purple. Pods commonly contain about 5–10 peas, though cultivar and maturity affect their size and number.

sections.title: Food
sections.text: Peas are eaten as seeds; some cultivars are harvested for their edible whole pods. Young shoots are also used as a vegetable.
